title: Artifact Acceptance Criteria
description:
What a dataset has to satisfy to serve as a given artifact: the variable it must carry, the units that variable may be in, the axes it must have, the grids it may be on, and any schema it must conform to.
**This is what makes `replace-with-local-equivalent` actionable.** That action is by far the most common in the FOCAL corpus, and on its own it says that something must change without saying what would count as having changed it correctly. A platform asked "can I run this workflow over my area of interest with my data?" cannot answer from the action alone. It can answer from these criteria, against a candidate file, with no human in the loop.
**These are properties of the artifact, not of the transfer.** UP-WF3's precipitation input needs millimetres or kg m⁻²s⁻¹ and a time axis whether or not anyone is moving the workflow anywhere; the requirement simply becomes visible when a substitution is proposed. So the criteria attach to the artifact declaration, where they are stated once, rather than to the rules that happen to invoke them. A rule saying `replace-with-local-equivalent` cites the artifact by id, and the criteria travel with it.
Every property is optional and at least one is required: a criteria object that only carries a note states no criterion. Where a requirement genuinely resists structuring, say it in `transferabilityNotes` rather than inventing a property for it.
**Published vocabularies, not FOCAL ones, wherever one exists.** Units are QUDT unit IRIs (`MilliM`, `KiloGM-PER-M2-SEC`, whose QUDT symbols are exactly the `mm` and `kg/(m²·s)` UP-WF3 states). A schema requirement is `dcterms:conformsTo`. Grid types are the same FOCAL scheme bblocks://ogc.focal.transferability.envelopeConstraint uses, cross-walked to CF `grid_mapping_name`. Only the variable entries and `axes` are FOCAL's own, and only because a workflow's internal expectation of what an input is called is not a published fact about anything.
**Evidenced 2/8:** UP-WF3 states the fullest contract in the corpus (variable name, either of two units, a time axis, one of two grids); UP-WF2 states the raster conventions its code assumes (variable name, packing, no-data). No current record uses `conformsTo`. Expect this to grow: the question was never asked in the questionnaires, so absence here is not evidence that other workflows have no contract.

name.description: The name the workflow expects the variable to be called. A plain string: a standard name says what a quantity is, this says what the code looks for.

sameAsCurrent.description: Instead of `name`: the variable must be called what the artifact currently in use calls it. For sources that state the requirement as that relation and never give a name; guessing a literal would assert something they did not say.

standardName.description: CF standard name of the quantity. Says what a name cannot, such as net against downwelling radiation. A list is **an OR-set**: any one is acceptable, e.g. a quantity accepted either as a flux or as an accumulation. Give it only where the quantity is certain.

units.description: Units the variable may be in, as QUDT unit IRIs (relative names resolve against `http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/`). **An OR-set:** any one is acceptable.

variables.description:
The variables the data must carry. **Conjunctive**: every entry must be satisfied. A single threshold value is one entry with only `units`.
The STAC datacube extension describes what a dataset contains; this states what a replacement must provide. The two correspond only partly.

axes.description: Axes the data must have, as concepts from the FOCAL axes scheme (see bblocks://ogc.focal.transferability.vocab). **Conjunctive**, unlike `units` and `gridTypes`: every axis listed must be present. UP-WF3 requires a time axis, without which its rolling accumulation has nothing to accumulate over.

gridTypes.description:
The grids the data may be on, from the same open scheme an envelope constraint's `grid-structure` dimension uses. **An OR-set.**
Not a duplicate of that dimension: the two do different jobs. An envelope constraint is a boundary a *rule is conditioned on* — cite it in `when` and the rule fires when the target falls outside it. These criteria are a specification a *candidate is checked against* once the rule has already fired and says to substitute something. State the constraint at the envelope when it bounds the workflow as a whole, and here when it binds this one artifact; UP-WF3 happens to be a case where both readings are available, because its only gridded input is also the whole of its gridded interface.

temporal.title: Time axis requirements

resolution.description: Required time step, as an ISO 8601 duration (`dcat:temporalResolution`).

calendar.description: CF `calendar` values accepted as they are. An OR-set. Say in `transferabilityNotes` what happens to the others, where the source does.

minimumPrecedingYears.description: Years of data needed **before** the requested period, e.g. 30 for a reference history.

complete.description: `true`: no gaps are allowed in the required data.

startDate.description: Start of the span the data must cover, as an ISO 8601 year, year-month or date (`dcat:startDate`). A requirement on the data, not the period for which results hold.

endDate.description: End of the span the data must cover (`dcat:endDate`). Optional; omit it where the source states only a start.

temporal.description: What the data's time axis must look like. Not the envelope's `temporal` dimension, which says for which period results hold.

conformsTo.description:
Schemas or specifications the data must conform to, as identifiers. Uplifts to `dcterms:conformsTo`, the term catalogues already use for exactly this.
No current record uses it. It was drafted for UP-WF2's planned Heat Risk Indicator (census data "preferably following a schema compatible with Eurostat's"), which the owners say is not part of the workflow today. Where a preference is genuinely soft, `transferabilityNotes` is the honest home for it.

transferabilityNotes.description: A requirement that does not reduce to the properties above, or a qualification on one that does. Uplifts to `rdfs:comment`. Mixed in from bblocks://ogc.focal.transferability.notes. Not a criterion on its own: a criteria object needs at least one structured property.
